Public Safety · NYC Open Data

238,421 collisions, turned into three deployment decisions

238,421 collisions analysed 635 fatalities identified 36.7% dangerous-collision rate

Built a Power Query model over 27 months of NYC motor vehicle collision records and separated a question everyone was asking wrong: the most common collision cause isn't the same as the most dangerous one. A single severity flag turned six raw casualty counts into one metric PivotTables could rank by risk, not just volume.

  • Friday 12PM–4PM is the single riskiest window in the week — a congestion problem, distinct from a separate weekend-overnight behavioural spike.
  • Failure to Yield Right-of-Way is the one factor that's both high-volume and high-severity (63.7% dangerous) — the priority over more common but less harmful causes.
  • Pedestrians are 8.1% of injuries but 45% of fatalities; Belt Parkway has a fatality rate 71% above the city average.
  • Delivered 4 recommendations mapped directly to evidence, including a fix for the 25% of records with no logged cause.
Power Query PivotTables Interactive Dashboard Severity Modelling Executive Storytelling
Logistics · Carrier & Warehouse Performance

2,000 shipments reveal ~$42K and 55 failures a year sitting on the table

2,000 shipments audited $401.9K freight spend benchmarked 7 carriers compared like-for-like

Xeenom Logistics tracked every shipment but never compared its seven carriers on the same axis. I built Cost-per-Mile and Distance-Bracket fields that made the seven carriers directly comparable for the first time, then mapped cost against reliability to show no single carrier wins on both.

  • UPS costs 24% more per mile than USPS, but is the only carrier with zero lost packages — the case for a tiered carrier policy, not a single supplier.
  • Amazon Logistics fails on 1 in 5 shipments — worst reliability at mid-tier cost.
  • San Francisco, Houston, and Atlanta warehouses fail nearly twice as often as New York, using the same carriers — a process gap, not a partner problem.
  • Distance and transit time correlate at 0.80, enough to quote SLAs by distance bracket instead of padding every promise.
Excel Data Modelling PivotTables Cost-per-Mile Analysis Slicer-Driven Dashboard
Retail · Sales & Shipping Performance

$742K in sales, mapped down to the city and shipping mode

$742.0K total sales tracked 8.0K units shipped 50 states mapped

Built a filterable sales overview across segment (Consumer, Corporate, Home Office) and region, pairing a U.S. shipping-distribution map with category and shipping-duration breakdowns so a category manager can move from a headline number to a root cause in two clicks.

  • Chairs is the top category at $328.4K, well ahead of Bookcases and Tables.
  • Sales grew 8% year-over-year, but profit fell 57% — a margin story hiding behind a growth headline.
  • December is peak sales month at $121,818; New York City leads all cities at $75.7K.
  • 59% of orders ship Second Class, with most deliveries completing in 4 days.
Excel Dashboard Design Geographic Mapping YoY Trend Analysis Segment Filtering
Personal Finance · Cash Flow Tracking

487 transactions, reconciled into one balance-sheet view

$65,440 income tracked $30,191 spending categorized 3 income streams reconciled

Designed a personal finance tracker that consolidates multiple income streams and categorized spending into a single monthly view, so a self-employed earner with irregular income can see cash flow trends at a glance instead of re-deriving them each month.

  • Rent is the single largest expense category at $9,000, ahead of groceries and clothing combined.
  • Income is concentrated in one primary stream ($50,000) supplemented by YouTube and Teachable revenue.
  • Monthly debit-vs-credit trend flags January as the heaviest spending month against income.
  • Weekly view shows spending peaks on Monday — useful for timing budget check-ins.

-- Create database for Smart city parking

CREATE DATABASE 
		Smart_City_Parking

USE Smart_City_Parking

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Next is to create the customer table and populate it!
CREATE TABLE Customers (
		Customer_id INT IDENTITY(1,1) PRIMARY KEY,
		First_name Varchar(100) NOT NULL,
		Last_name Varchar(100) NOT NULL,
		Phone_num Nvarchar(15) NULL UNIQUE,
		Email NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
		Address NVARCHAR(150) NOT NULL
);
GO

-- Create Metadata
ALTER TABLE Customers
ADD 
		CreatedAt DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT GETDATE(),
		UpdatedAt DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT GETDATE()
GO

SELECT * FROM customers

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
--CREATE vehicle table and also populate it!
CREATE TABLE Vehicle (
		vehicle_id INT IDENTITY(1,1) PRIMARY KEY,
		customer_id INT NOT NULL,
		license_plate NVARCHAR(10) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
		make NVARCHAR (100) NOT NULL, 
		model NVARCHAR (100) NOT NULL, 
		color NVARCHAR (100) NOT NULL, 
		vehicle_type NVARCHAR (100) NOT NULL,

-- Create Metadata
CreatedAt DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT GETDATE(),
UpdatedAt DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT GETDATE(),

--Connect customer table with vehicle id

CONSTRAINT FK_Vehicle_CustomerID
		FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES Customers (customer_id)
);
GO

SELECT * FROM Vehicle

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
--Create parking lot table
CREATE TABLE Parking_Lot (
		Parkinglot_Id INT IDENTITY(1,1) PRIMARY KEY,
		Name NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL, 
		Address NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL, 
		City_zone NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL, 
		Total_spaces INT NOT NULL,
		hourly_rate DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL
);
GO	

SELECT * FROM Parking_Lot

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
--Create Parking spaces
CREATE TABLE Parking_Spaces (
		space_id INT IDENTITY(1,1) PRIMARY KEY,
		Space_number NVARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,
		floor_level NVARCHAR(10),
		Parkinglot_Id INT NOT NULL,
		space_type NVARCHAR(10) NOT NULL CHECK (space_type IN('regular', 'compact', 'handicap', 'electric')),
		occupied BIT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
		CONSTRAINT FK_lot_space
FOREIGN KEY (Parkinglot_Id) REFERENCES Parking_Lot (Parkinglot_Id),
UNIQUE( Parkinglot_Id, Space_number) 
);


SELECT * FROM Parking_Spaces
GO

--Create Parking Sessions
CREATE TABLE Parking_sessions (
		session_id INT IDENTITY(1,1) PRIMARY KEY,
	-- Connecting tables
		Customer_id INT NOT NULL,
		vehicle_id INT NOT NULL,
		space_id INT NOT NULL,
	--Table creations
		vehicle_enters DATETIME NULL,
		vehicle_exits DATETIME NULL,
	--Create the hour and rate table
		total_hours AS (DATEDIFF(HOUR, vehicle_enters, vehicle_exits)),
		total_fee AS (DATEDIFF(HOUR, vehicle_enters, vehicle_exits)* 5),
		payment_status NVARCHAR(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unpaid' CHECK (payment_status IN ('unpaid', 'paid')),
	--Creating a foreign key for the connecting tables
FOREIGN KEY (vehicle_id) REFERENCES Vehicle (vehicle_id),
FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES Customers (customer_id),
FOREIGN KEY (space_id) REFERENCES Parking_spaces (space_id)
);
GO

SELECT * FROM Parking_sessions


--Create Membership plans
CREATE TABLE Membership_plan (
	plan_id INT IDENTITY(1,1) PRIMARY KEY,
	plan_type NVARCHAR(20) NOT NULL CHECK (plan_type IN ('Monthly', 'Quarterly','Yearly')),
	plan_name NVARCHAR(20) NOT NULL CHECK (plan_name IN('Residential', 'Commercial', 'Restricted')),
	plan_price DECIMAL(4,2) NOT NULL,
	validity_period INT NOT NULL,
	discount_percentage DECIMAL (5,2) NOT NULL
	);

	ALTER TABLE Membership_plan
ALTER COLUMN plan_price DECIMAL(6,2) NOT NULL
GO

	Select* FROM Membership_plan

-- connecting table
CREATE TABLE Customers_plan(
	customer_plan INT IDENTITY(1,1) NOT NULL,
	plan_id INT NOT NULL,
	customer_id INT NOT NULL,

-- Creating date and time table to monitor duration of plan
	startdate DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT GETDATE(),
	enddate DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT GETDATE(),

-- Connect foreign keys
	FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES Customers(customer_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (plan_id) REFERENCES Membership_Plan(plan_id)
);


SELECT * FROM Customers_plan

Database Design · SQL Server

A relational schema that runs a 5-lot, 50-space city parking network

6 normalized tables 50 spaces across 5 lots 9 membership plans modelled

Designed and built a full T-SQL schema for a smart-city parking system from scratch — customers, vehicles, lots, spaces, sessions, and membership plans — rather than just querying data someone else had already structured.

  • Computed columns (total_hours, total_fee) calculate billing directly from entry/exit timestamps, so fees never need manual entry.
  • CHECK constraints enforce valid space types (regular / compact / handicap / electric) and payment status at the database level, not in application code.
  • NULL exit timestamps model live, in-progress sessions — the same table tracks history and current occupancy without a separate status field.
  • Foreign keys tie customers to tiered plans (Monthly/Quarterly/Yearly × Residential/Commercial/Restricted) with built-in discount logic.

-- Fix a text column before it can be aggregated
ALTER TABLE customer
ALTER COLUMN age TYPE INT USING age::INTEGER;

-- Segment customers worth a closer look
SELECT * FROM customer
WHERE age > 50 AND segment = 'Home Office';

-- Reshape order_date into reportable fields
SELECT order_date,
    TO_CHAR(order_date, 'Day')   AS day_name,
    TO_CHAR(order_date, 'Month') AS month_name
FROM sales;

-- Compare order volume by shipping mode
SELECT ship_mode, COUNT(sales) AS no_of_sales
FROM sales
GROUP BY ship_mode;

Cleaning, filtering, and segmenting a retail dataset directly in SQL

Worked directly against a customer / product / sales schema — fixing a mis-typed column before it could be aggregated correctly, then moving through filtering, grouping, and date-based reporting to answer specific business questions without exporting to Excel first.

  • Converted age from text to integer with USING age::INTEGER before any numeric filtering or averaging would work.
  • Segmented customers by combined conditions — e.g. age over 50 and segment = Home Office — using AND/OR/IN/BETWEEN/NOT.
  • Extracted day, month, and year from order dates with EXTRACT and TO_CHAR for time-based reporting.
  • Aggregated shipment volume and quantity by ship mode and region using COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN/MAX with GROUP BY.
